text: Every endpoint in this service has to check the data it receives.
We are obliged to validate user input before it reaches the handler.
A new form cannot be merged until its fields are validated.
Validating input is non-negotiable; no team gets a waiver.
Under no circumstances may unchecked data enter the system, even for internal callers.
Skipping input checks is never acceptable, not even for a hotfix.
You may add extra checks on incoming fields if you find them useful.
Go ahead and validate inputs in the client as well, that is allowed.
Teams are welcome to introduce their own input checks.
There is no need to validate values that our own compiler generated.
This internal script can ship without checking its arguments.
Nobody is asking you to verify input in the throwaway prototype.
Do not validate input inside the database layer.
Adding input checks to the generated client is forbidden.
We have banned ad hoc validation in the view templates.
List endpoints have to return their results in pages.
Any query that returns many rows needs to be paginated.
The review will block a collection API that lacks page parameters.
Returning an unbounded list is never tolerated, whatever the deadline.
Paging is non-negotiable on every collection endpoint, internal ones included.
No exemption will be granted: results are paged, full stop.
Feel free to page the audit view if it helps.
The export screen is allowed to split its results into pages.
You may offer cursor paging on this endpoint.
The country list is tiny, so there is no need to page it.
This endpoint can return everything at once without page support.
We do not insist on paging for the settings screen.
Do not paginate the full data export.
Splitting the ledger download into pages is forbidden.
Page parameters are banned on the snapshot endpoint.
Public APIs have to throttle each client.
Our gateway is obliged to cap the request rate per key.
A new external endpoint needs a request quota before launch.
The login route is throttled without exception; nobody can switch it off.
Capping request rates is non-negotiable, even for our biggest customer.
Never expose an unthrottled public route, no matter who asks.
You may throttle the reporting endpoint if load becomes a problem.
Teams are allowed to set their own request quotas.
It is fine to cap traffic on the sandbox.
Internal health probes do not need a request cap.
The admin tool can go live without throttling.
There is no obligation to limit request rates in the test environment.
Do not throttle the payment callback.
Placing a request cap on the emergency endpoint is forbidden.
We have ruled out per-client quotas on the internal event bus.
Any change to a table has to go through a migration script.
Releases that alter columns need an accompanying migration.
The team is obliged to migrate the schema before deploying this model.
Altering tables outside a migration is never excused, even during an incident.
Every structural database change goes through a migration, with zero waivers.
It is non-negotiable that the schema evolves only through migration files.
You are welcome to restructure the tables in this release.
A migration may be included in the patch version.
Changing the database layout during this sprint is allowed.
Adding this index needs no migration step.
The feature can ship while the old table layout stays untouched.
Nobody has to migrate the scratch database.
Do not run schema changes during the sales freeze.
Migrating the legacy tables is forbidden.
Structural changes to the shared database are banned for this team.
New checkout behaviour has to sit behind a flag.
Risky changes need a feature toggle before release.
We are obliged to gate this rollout with a flag.
Unflagged launches are never tolerated, however small the change.
Gating new behaviour behind a toggle is non-negotiable for every team.
No release manager can waive the feature flag on payment changes.
Feel free to hide the new banner behind a toggle.
You may use flags to stage this change.
Wrapping the experiment in a switch is allowed.
A copy fix does not need a toggle.
This bug fix can go out without a feature switch.
There is no need to flag changes to the developer docs.
Do not put the security patch behind a toggle.
Feature switches in the cryptography module are forbidden.
We have banned new flags in the billing core.
The consumer has to discard repeated events.
Imported contacts need duplicate removal before saving.
We are obliged to filter out repeated messages in this pipeline.
A duplicate charge is never acceptable, so repeats are filtered without exception.
Removing repeated records is non-negotiable in the ledger feed.
No source is exempt from duplicate filtering, whatever its reputation.
You may collapse identical log lines.
It is fine to drop repeated alerts if they get noisy.
The importer is allowed to merge duplicate rows.
The source already guarantees unique records, so there is no need to filter repeats.
This job can run without removing duplicates.
Nobody expects duplicate filtering from the debug stream.
Do not deduplicate the audit trail.
Merging repeated transactions is forbidden.
Dropping identical events from the raw archive is banned.
Writes to the warehouse have to be grouped into batches.
The sync job needs to send records in bulk.
We are obliged to combine these calls into grouped requests.
Sending rows one at a time is never accepted here, even for a single customer.
Grouping writes is non-negotiable for every producer, with no waiver.
No caller gets to bypass bulk submission, whatever the urgency.
You may group the notifications into one request.
Bulk inserts are allowed if they simplify the code.
Feel free to buffer events and send them together.
Low-volume jobs do not need to group their writes.
This worker can send records individually; bulk mode is not something we ask for.
There is no need to buffer these calls.
Do not batch password reset messages.
Grouping payment authorisations into one call is forbidden.
Bulk submission to the partner API is banned.
Analytics datasets have to be stripped of personal identity.
We are obliged to anonymise records before sharing them.
A research export needs identities removed first.
Identifiable data never leaves the vault, and no executive can override that.
Anonymising shared records is non-negotiable in every single case.
No deadline justifies releasing data that still identifies people.
You may anonymise the demo dataset if you like.
Removing identities from internal reports is allowed.
Teams are welcome to scrub names from their samples.
Synthetic records do not need identities removed.
This report can use the data as it is, without anonymising it.
There is no obligation to scrub aggregate totals.
Do not anonymise the legal hold copy.
Stripping identities from the fraud investigation records is forbidden.
We have banned anonymising data in the billing system.
Breaking changes have to ship under a new API version.
Public endpoints need a version number.
We are obliged to version this interface before partners use it.
Changing a published contract without a new version is never excused.
Versioning the public API is non-negotiable, for every partner and every release.
No team may be exempted from putting versions on external interfaces.
You may introduce a second version of the internal API.
It is fine to number the experimental endpoints.
Adding a version prefix to this route is allowed.
An internal function call does not need a version scheme.
This additive change can be released without a new API version.
There is no need to number the private endpoints.
Do not create another version of the authentication API.
Adding version prefixes to the webhook paths is forbidden.
We have ruled out maintaining parallel API versions.
Each service has to expose a liveness endpoint.
The load balancer needs a readiness probe from every instance.
New workers are obliged to report their health.
A service without a health probe is never deployed, without a single exception.
Health reporting is non-negotiable, even for temporary services.
No waiver exists for liveness probes in production.
You may add a deeper readiness probe.
Exposing a status endpoint on the batch tool is allowed.
Feel free to report dependency health too.
A one-off script does not need a status endpoint.
This job can run without any liveness probe.
There is no need for readiness reporting on the local mock.
Do not add a health endpoint to the public gateway.
Probing the licensed third-party server for status is forbidden.
Dependency checks inside the liveness probe are banned.
The customer database has to be copied to a safe place on a schedule.
Each production store needs a backup plan.
We are obliged to keep recoverable copies of this data.
Running production without recoverable copies is never acceptable, whatever the cost.
Backing up the ledger is non-negotiable and cannot be waived by anyone.
No environment holding customer data is exempt from being backed up.
You may take an extra snapshot before the upgrade.
Copying the development database for safekeeping is allowed.
Feel free to back up your sandbox.
The cache can be rebuilt, so there is no need to back it up.
Scratch tables can live without any backup.
Nobody has to snapshot the test fixtures.
Do not back up the decrypted secrets.
Copying session tokens into snapshots is forbidden.
Taking backups of the restricted dataset onto laptops is banned.
Changes have to be reviewed by a colleague before merging.
Each pull request needs a second pair of eyes.
We are obliged to get approval from a reviewer on this repository.
Nobody merges unreviewed code, not even the most senior engineer during an outage.
Peer review is non-negotiable for every commit to the main branch.
No change is exempt from a reviewer, however trivial.
You may ask a colleague to look over your prototype.
Requesting an extra reviewer is allowed.
Feel free to have another team read the change.
Automated dependency bumps do not need a human reviewer.
Your personal experiment branch can be merged without anyone reading it.
There is no need for peer approval on typo fixes in notes.
Do not send the embargoed security fix to the public review queue.
Authors are forbidden from approving their own changes through the review tool.
Review of the vendored third-party sources is ruled out; nobody is to open such requests.
The new service has to be tested under heavy traffic before launch.
A capacity change needs a stress run.
We are obliged to measure how it behaves at peak volume.
Launching without a stress run is never allowed, even if marketing has announced the date.
Testing at peak traffic is non-negotiable for all customer-facing services.
No release on the checkout path skips performance testing, without exception.
You may stress the staging cluster this week.
Running a traffic simulation on the new endpoint is allowed.
Feel free to benchmark it under load.
A documentation site does not need a stress run.
This small internal tool can launch without being tested under traffic.
There is no need to simulate peak volume for a config change.
Do not generate stress traffic against the production database.
Hammering a partner's servers with simulated users is forbidden.
Peak traffic simulations are banned during business hours.
Card numbers have to be hidden on support screens.
Logs that show account details need the sensitive parts obscured.
We are obliged to mask personal fields in this view.
A full card number is never displayed to anyone, with no override for managers.
Obscuring secrets in output is non-negotiable in every environment.
No screen is exempt from hiding sensitive fields, whatever the support case.
You may blur names in the demo screenshots.
Hiding part of the email address in this list is allowed.
Feel free to obscure internal identifiers too.
Public product codes do not need to be hidden.
This table can show the values in full, masking is unnecessary.
There is no obligation to obscure fake test data.
Do not mask the fields in the regulator's evidence export.
Obscuring the transaction reference is forbidden.
We have banned partial hiding of values in the reconciliation report.
Calls to the settlement service have to carry a signature.
Webhooks we send need to be cryptographically signed.
We are obliged to sign outgoing API calls.
An unsigned payment call is never accepted, and nobody can disable the check.
Signing requests is non-negotiable between all of our services.
No integration partner is exempt from signed calls, without exception.
You may sign requests to the internal metrics service.
Adding a signature header to these calls is allowed.
Feel free to sign the sandbox traffic.
Public read-only calls do not need a signature.
The local mock accepts traffic without any signing.
There is no need to sign calls that stay inside one process.
Do not sign requests with the root key.
Attaching signatures to calls sent to the legacy proxy is forbidden.
Client-side signing in the browser is banned.
Third-party libraries have to be locked to exact versions.
The build needs a lock file with fixed releases.
We are obliged to pin every package this service imports.
Floating versions are never tolerated in production builds, for any library.
Locking dependency versions is non-negotiable, even for a quick patch.
No package escapes the version lock, whatever its maintainer promises.
You may fix the versions in your example project.
Locking this development tool to one release is allowed.
Feel free to freeze the packages for the demo.
A throwaway notebook does not need locked library versions.
This sample can depend on the latest releases without a lock file.
There is no need to freeze versions of the linters.
Do not pin the security scanner to an old release.
Freezing the certificate bundle at one version is forbidden.
Exact version locks are banned in our published library.
Every release has to have a way back to the previous version.
A deployment plan needs a tested revert step.
We are obliged to be able to undo this change.
Shipping something that cannot be reverted is never permissible, even under pressure.
A working path back is non-negotiable for every production deployment.
No release is excused from being reversible, without exception.
You may revert the release if the graphs look odd.
Undoing yesterday's deployment is allowed.
Feel free to go back to the earlier build.
A static page update does not need a revert plan.
This experiment can be deployed without preparing a way back.
There is no need to rehearse undoing the config tweak.
Do not revert the database upgrade once data has been written.
Going back to the vulnerable build is forbidden.
Automatic undo of payment releases is banned.
The events table has to be split across several database nodes.
At this volume the store needs to be partitioned by customer.
We are obliged to distribute tenant data over separate shards.
Keeping all tenants on one node is never acceptable for this system, no matter the quarter.
Partitioning the ledger across nodes is non-negotiable and cannot be deferred.
No large table is exempt from being split between servers.
You may partition the metrics store if it grows.
Splitting this collection across nodes is allowed.
Feel free to distribute the search index.
A table of a few thousand rows does not need partitioning.
The service can run on a single node without splitting its data.
There is no need to distribute the lookup tables.
Do not split the accounting database across nodes.
Partitioning the configuration store is forbidden.
We have banned manual shards in application code.
Old methods have to tell callers they are going away.
Before removing an endpoint we need to announce it with a warning.
We are obliged to emit a notice when the legacy function is used.
Nothing is removed without prior notice to callers, and no maintainer can waive that.
Warning users of retiring features is non-negotiable in every library release.
No public symbol is exempt from a sunset notice, whatever the schedule.
You may log a notice when the old flag is used.
Adding a sunset message to the internal helper is allowed.
Feel free to warn callers ahead of time.
An unreleased method can be removed without any sunset notice.
Private helpers do not need to warn before they disappear.
There is no need to announce removal of dead test code.
Do not print sunset notices in the command's machine-readable output.
Emitting removal warnings from the hot loop is forbidden.
We have banned deprecation messages in the stable branch.
Database clients have to reuse connections from a shared pool.
The service needs a connection pool before it takes traffic.
We are obliged to pool our sessions to the database.
Opening a fresh connection per query is never accepted, in any service.
Reusing pooled connections is non-negotiable, with no carve-out for batch jobs.
No client of the primary database is exempt from pooling.
You may keep a pool of HTTP connections here.
Sharing sessions through a pool is allowed in this worker.
Feel free to reuse connections to the cache.
A nightly script does not need a connection pool.
This tool can open a single connection and skip pooling.
There is no need to pool calls to the local file store.
Do not pool connections that carry user-specific credentials.
Reusing sessions across tenants through a pool is forbidden.
Connection pools are banned in the serverless handler.
